solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Self-employed fishmonger?

definitions.meaning: a one-person business, someone working for themselves with no partners
playfully, a dealer in one kind of flatfish; the question mark flags the whimsy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a self-employed fish seller counts as a small business.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-person business is the standard British term for a self-employed trader; the fish sense is a pun on the flatfish.

clue.text: Pop's son and daughter first and second

indicators.note: first and second means the opening two letters of each of the words son and daughter

explanation.surface: Dad's son and daughter come first and second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like Dad, with the 's of possession, but it is the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a common name for a fizzy soft drink, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Stand base of vessel on three-quarters of concrete mix

indicators.note: on means placed on top of the following piece in a down answer
in a down clue the base of a word is its last letter
mix says the remaining letters are stirred up
three-quarters of keeps six of the eight letters of concrete, dropping the first two

explanation.surface: Instructions for standing a vessel's base on a concrete mix.
explanation.walkthrough: Concrete without CO leaves NCRETE, mixed into ECTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading desk in a church is a stand for holding a book.

clue.text: End sharply with E-chord resonating — the essence of stereo for analogue audio equipment

indicators.note: with joins the second piece after the first

parts.note: to taper is to narrow to a point

indicators.note: resonating means sounding, so the chord is heard and written as cord

parts.note: a chord of E, which when spoken is the letter E plus a word for string

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so the middle letters of stereo

explanation.surface: A musician ends sharply on an E chord ringing through stereo speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of STEREO is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that records sound onto magnetic tape is classic analogue audio gear.

clue.text: Burning car in collision with truck west of Evesham

indicators.note: in collision with means running into, so the truck comes right up against the car

parts.note: auto is a short word for a motor car
DAF is a Dutch truck manufacturer

indicators.note: in an across reading, the west of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A burning car after a crash with a lorry near the town of Evesham.
explanation.walkthrough: Evesham is a market town in Worcestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An auto-da-fé was the burning of a heretic after sentence by the Inquisition.

clue.text: Tempt with magnificent iced filling

indicators.note: filling is what lies inside, so the letters sit within the two words

explanation.surface: A cake temptation with a gorgeous iced filling.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone towards something is to tempt them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Former athlete's endless muscle pain

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the muscle-pain word is cut off

parts.note: a cramp is a painful muscle spasm

explanation.surface: A retired runner suffers from a muscle pain that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a British middle-distance runner of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Cram, the British miler and world champion, is a retired track star.

clue.text: Put new gloss on a Pinter play

indicators.note: play suggests the letters move freely, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A director gives a Harold Pinter play a fresh interpretation.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying fresh coats of gloss paint is what redoing paintwork means.

clue.text: Very occasional pieces covering unfortunate final Foreman-Ali upset

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the pieces word goes round the unfortunate word

parts.note: men are the pieces in chess or draughts
ill means unlucky, as in ill fortune

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of the boxer's name
upset means knocked over, so the letters of Ali are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxing upset in the final between Foreman and Ali, a rare fight indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: George Foreman and Muhammad Ali fought the 'Rumble in the Jungle' in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once every thousand years is extremely infrequent.

clue.text: Make Bill sick?

parts.note: removing the head of the word Bill leaves the word ill, so beheading turns Bill sick

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how to make a man named Bill unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the B off Bill and he becomes ILL: cutting off the head is what makes him sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To behead someone is to cut off their head, which is exactly what turns the word Bill into ill.

clue.text: Drop half a pound or a stone

indicators.note: half here takes the second two of the four letters of drop

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A weight question: lose half a pound or a whole stone?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop half' looks like an instruction to lose weight, but it means half the word Drop (OP). Pound and stone are both British weights; stone is fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an iridescent gemstone, so it is an example of a precious stone.

clue.text: Drop stories about latest sexist outburst? That's his job!

definitions.text: Drop stories about latest sexist outburst? That's his job!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the final letter of sexist
outburst suggests the words are blown apart and rearranged
latest picks the last letter of sexist

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor spikes stories about a sexist rant, all part of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop stories is jumbled and T, from sexist, goes inside; a sports desk is notorious for such outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: The journalist in charge of the sports pages decides which stories run and which are dropped.

clue.text: In retrospect double-entendre elicited a sly look

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
In says the letters sit inside the run of the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking back, a saucy double meaning drew a knowing glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'In retrospect' to the reversal alone; 'In' is the hidden-word signal and 'retrospect' the reversal, so each operation has its own word.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestive sidelong glance, often lecherous, is what this word means.

clue.text: Crafty attempt to dupe ref is entertaining except with No.10 getting dismissed

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: in football a dive is a faked fall to fool the referee

indicators.note: getting dismissed says the ten letter is sent off from the word except

parts.note: taken as written
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A footballer's crafty dive fools the referee, except when the number ten is sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No.10' looks like a shirt number but is the Roman numeral X; 'getting dismissed' removes it from the word except.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misleading or designed to trick is crafty, a close synonym.

clue.text: Bold challenger's lead evaporated during shambolic chorus

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other
shambolic means chaotic, so the letters of chorus are disordered
lead evaporated says the first letter vanishes

parts.note: a challenger is a rival

explanation.surface: A daring challenger loses the lead in a chaotic chorus line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead evaporated' strips the first letter of the challenger word; 'shambolic' scrambles chorus around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Knightly behaviour includes bravery, so gallant daring is part of the sense.

clue.text: Prior to strike worker shows restraint

indicators.note: prior to means the worker piece comes before the strike piece

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the open hand

explanation.surface: Before striking, a worker shows self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows restraint' reads as a phrase about calm, but 'shows' is a link and 'restraint' a noun for the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuff locked around the wrist is a device for restraining a prisoner.

clue.text: Surrealist Bronte novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the name's letters are rearranged afresh

explanation.surface: A surreal novel by one of the Brontë sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by a Brontë but signals an anagram of BRONTE.
explanation.definitionFit: André Breton was the French poet who founded the Surrealist movement.

clue.text: Recall deep drug treatment

indicators.note: treatment means working on, so the letters are handled into a new order

explanation.surface: Remembering a powerful drug therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig out something long buried, such as an old memory, is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: Gavaskar's boundaries follow by means of a therapy for recapturing past form

indicators.note: follow says the boundary letters come after the by-means-of word

parts.note: via means through or by means of

indicators.note: boundaries are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of the name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer hoping to regain old form tries some therapy after hitting boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunil Gavaskar is a famous Indian batsman; in cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the edge of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug for erectile dysfunction is, humorously, a treatment for regaining past performance.

clue.text: Musicians playing with lack of inhibition

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
on means playing or performing, as on stage

explanation.surface: A group of musicians performs with wild abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with complete freedom from restraint is doing it wildly, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Following No.1 in India, Chris Rea's topped all over the place — this includes Isle of Man!

indicators.note: following says the jumbled letters come after the India letter
the number one letter of a word is its first letter
all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged
topped means each word loses its top letter

parts.note: the singer's name with its possessive, Chris Rea's

explanation.surface: Singer Chris Rea, after topping the charts in India, tours everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' beheads both words: HRIS and EAS. Jumbled after I they make the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man sits in the stretch of water between Britain and Ireland that bears this name.

clue.text: See 24
According to Spooner, environmentalist's opponent to give up

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: Al Gore is a prominent environmental campaigner
a foe is an enemy or opponent

explanation.surface: An environmentalist's opponent gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: Gore foe, swapped by sound, becomes fore go.
explanation.definitionFit: To do without something or abstain is to give it up.

clue.text: Lack of central heating in Dales hotel affected tenure

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters are reordered
lack of says a letter is missing from the hotel letters
central picks the middle letter of the word heating

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire Dales hotel with no central heating is having an effect on its guests' stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central heating' looks like a radiator system but means the middle letter of heating, T, which comes out of DALES HOTEL before the rest is rearranged. The Dales are hill country in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A property held on a lease for a set term is a form of land tenure.

clue.text: Dreadful, dreadful artists in great distress

parts.note: dire means dreadful or terrible

indicators.note: dreadful again, now saying the artists are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Terrible painters find themselves in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits were also a British rock band, so the artists are a fitting cameo.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in this state is an idiom for being in serious difficulty or trouble.

clue.text: Coming from Provencal city in which criminal interest has been eradicated

indicators.note: eradicated means wiped out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Avignon is a city in Provence
vig, or vigorish, is the interest a loan shark charges

explanation.surface: From a Provençal city where loan-sharking has been stamped out.
explanation.definitionFit: This word means soon, shortly, so it suits something that is on its way.

clue.text: Such characters sent back through side door

definitions.text: Such characters sent back through side door

indicators.note: sent back says those letters are read in reverse order
the characters in question are the odd-numbered letters of side door

explanation.surface: Shady types are turned away through the side door.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of side door are S, D, D, O; read backwards they spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd-placed letters are exactly the characters the clue picks, and odd characters can mean strange people.

clue.text: Lame steed run in dreadful pain is not mounted

indicators.note: in places the steed letters inside the pain letters
dreadful means badly made, so the letters of pain are scrambled
lame suggests something hobbled and out of order, so the letters of steed are mixed

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A lame horse in awful pain cannot be ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lame' wants to be the definition (pedestrian also means dull) but it is the anagram signal for steed; 'dreadful' scrambles pain, which then holds those letters plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling on foot, rather than on horseback, is a walker, not riding.

clue.text: Dip and alternative to dip

definitions.meaning: to dip is to go down or drop lower
in the phrase about surviving, the choice is to swim or the opposite; a dip is a swim

explanation.surface: A dip, or something else instead of a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinking is dropping down, and the stock phrase pairs swimming with going under as the two options.

clue.text: Firm with million plus capital working for association

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
Paris is the capital of France
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A company with a million in capital is up and running.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparing two things links them in the mind, so association is a loose synonym for setting one beside another.
